intro.text: The capital of Idris: a quiet place of just a few thousand people, hardly more than a village beside the great cities of other lands.

description.text: Only a short stretch of summer is warm; the rest of the year is cold. Homes are thatched cottages built with sturdy whitewashed stone, and the dirt roads turn to mud.

The royal palace is a broad building of one storey, with squat walls under a peaked wooden roof. Its stables open onto a courtyard of packed earth with a gate to the outside, and crowds often haggle near the main door. It is big enough to seem a little showy, which people forgive because it also serves as a meeting hall.
Besides housing the royal family, the palace is where the kingdom's leaders gather and its affairs are run.
The town lies in a valley among the Idrian mountains, several weeks' travel from the southern farms, which some call the lower farms.

items.text: Some three centuries after the Manywar, General Yarda brought a bright pink letter to Bevalis: Idris was expected to send a princess south to wed the God King of Hallandren.
King Dedelin chose his youngest daughter, Siri, and sent her off with soldiers, a steward, a few serving boys and the finest carriage Idris owned.
